title: Agentic Turtles High-Stakes Confirmation Record
description: The decision ledger for one high-stakes plan step, committed at confirmations/<workload>/<step-id>.json on the default branch. Its LATEST decision about the step being built is what unblocks or blocks the build, even on an approved, frozen plan (FR-023, FR-024, SC-006). Each decision is BOUND to the work it was given about: the workload it belongs to, and a digest of the step's own content (amended 2026-08-17, GHI #95) — an authority's answer authorizes THAT step in THAT workload and nothing else. A LEDGER rather than a single answer (amended 2026-08-27, GHI #96): the record used to say only that a conversation happened, with no field for what was decided, so a recorded refusal read as a confirmation and unblocked the build it should have stopped. Entries are appended, never rewritten — each names its own author, so lifting a block does not edit the authority's answer. Append-only is a convention here, not a structural guarantee: git history is the audit trail, and this schema does not make a rewritten entry detectable.

step_id.description: The plan step this ledger is about; must equal the <step-id> in the filename (the record is looked up by it)

workload.description: The workload slug this ledger belongs to; must equal the <workload> directory in the path. Step ids are unique only WITHIN a plan, so without this two workloads that both declare step-billing-cycle would share one record and one authority's answer would unblock the other's build (GHI #95).

authority.description: Must equal the step's authority (FR-023 names the route, FR-024 makes it binding). Extensible in future schema versions. A re-route is a different question, not the same one, so it is compared before the digest — see confirmationVerdict.

decisions.description: In chronological order, oldest first. `at` must be non-decreasing. An `overridden` entry must be preceded by a `rejected` entry carrying the SAME step_digest — an override of nothing is a mis-recorded approval wearing the word.

Decision.description: One decision about one version of the step. Uniform shape whoever made it: an authority answering, or an operator lifting a block they recorded.

decision.description: `approved` and `rejected` are the authority's answer. `overridden` is the OPERATOR lifting a recorded refusal — a deliberate, attributable act that the gate reports loudly rather than silently passing (FR-024, GHI #96).

step_digest.description: sha256 over the step's id, intent, acceptance and authority, canonically serialized — WHICH VERSION of the step this decision was about. Per entry rather than per record (2026-08-27) so a ledger survives a step revision: the gate reads the newest entry matching the CURRENT step, and an earlier version's answer stays as history without authorizing anything. Obtain it from the review page's high-stakes panel — it prints the entry to commit with this field filled in.

at.description: ISO 8601 / RFC 3339 instant, zone included — either a Z suffix or a numeric offset. Decisions are expected AFTER the plan is frozen (FR-024), so the moment is part of the record.

rationale.description: For `approved`/`rejected`: the guardrails actually confirmed or the ground for refusing, in the authority's terms. For `overridden`: why the block was lifted. Must carry non-whitespace text — a blank rationale decides nothing while still moving the gate.

Attribution.description: Named person/org + contact context — both halves are what make an entry attributable. A name nobody can reach cannot be corroborated afterwards; a contact with no name attributes the decision to no one.

Legacy.description: The pre-ledger shape, still accepted and read as a ledger of exactly one `approved` entry (constitution Frozen-Artifact Compatibility, route (a)). This is not a guess made to keep old data working: refusal was UNREPRESENTABLE when these records were written, so every one of them is necessarily an approval. Writers emit the ledger shape; this branch exists only so records committed before 2026-08-27 keep verifying.
